newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish lira at 100,500 vs dlr on official cb mkt.
newsitem.headline: Turkish lira at 100,500 vs dlr on official cb mkt.

text.p: The Turkish lira hit 100,500 psychological level against the dollar on the official, central bank-monitored interbank market at midday, easing from Friday's 99,645 close due to a higher dollar/mark parity in world markets.
Bankers said the currency trade was quiet and the lira was not much changed from opening levels due continuing cash squeeze in the money market.
Bankers said the lira firmed slightly after the opening as the 73.2 trillion lira cash shortage dominated the market and forced banks to sell dollars for lira.
The central bank lent banks more than nine trillion lira overnight money at 80 percent on Monday morning to meet cash demand. Overnight money also traded at 79.75 percent.

"The central bank did not open a repo auction to relieve the cash squeeze, but is injecting cash via overnight lending. The currency market is quiet and banks are mostly on the selling side," a banker said.

"We did not see any immediate reaction to the piercing of the 100,000 psychological level, but some dollar demand may arise from the free currency market now that the lira has exceeded 100,000," she added.
The lira has lost 4.8 percent of its value against the dollar so far this month, after a 4.5 percent loss in the whole of October.
The lira's depreciation rate against the dollar was around 41 percent since the beginning of 1996, after a 35 percent depreciation in the whole of 1995.
T-bill and bond yields were little changed from Friday levels despite cash shortage.
The yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper stood at 119.02 percent, unchanged from Friday.
